mainTopic: The fate of the ארון after the חורבן, how its poles were seen through the פרוכת, and the showing of the כרובים to ישראל on the רגל
overview: This עמוד asks what happened to the ארון when the מקדש ראשון was destroyed. One view says it went into exile, reading 'כל הדרה' as 'her chamber.' רבי שמעון בן יוחי says it was hidden in its place, because the פסוק about its poles says 'they are there to this day.' רבה challenges עולא from the יבוסי, where 'to this day' cannot mean forever. עולא's answer, that the extra word 'שם' means forever, is refuted from בני שמעון, whom סנחריב exiled. The חכמים say the ארון was hidden under the floor of the לשכת דיר העצים, and a משנה tells of a כהן who found the spot and died. The גמרא then explains how the poles were 'seen and not seen': they pressed the פרוכת out like a woman's breasts. רב קטינא says the כרובים were shown to the people on the רגל as a sign of ה׳'s love. The גמרא defends this with the parable of a bride, and then asks which מקדש he meant, giving two answers: the gate curtains of the מקדש ראשון, or carved כרובים on the walls of the מקדש שני. The explanation of 'כמער איש ולויות' continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: 'All her splendor' means 'her chamber'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes the verse 'ויצא מבת ציון כל הדרה' and reads הדרה (splendor) as חדרה (her chamber). The point is that the hidden treasure of the inner chamber, the ארון, went out into exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...all her splendor.' What does 'all her splendor' mean? It means 'her chamber.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the proof for the opinion that the ארון was taken to בבל. It reads the word הדרה as if it said חדרה, 'her chamber.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that 'all her splendor' left בת ציון. By reading הדרה as חדרה, the ברייתא turns a general line about lost glory into a statement about the innermost room, the קודש הקדשים. So the thing in that chamber, the ארון, left with the exile.

keyTerms.meaning: Her chamber, the inner room (the קודש הקדשים)

steps.confusionAlert: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle of a quote. The words 'כל הדרה' are the end of a פסוק (איכה א:ו) that began on the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: "...all her splendor."
phrases.notes: End of the פסוק from איכה א:ו, begun on the previous עמוד

phrases.english: What is 'all her splendor'?
Her chamber.
phrases.notes: A play on the similar sound of הדרה and חדרה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the scriptural proof begun on the previous עמוד for the view that the ארון was exiled.
steps.raayaObject: The ארון went into exile in בבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: איכה א:ו, 'ויצא מבת ציון כל הדרה,' read as 'חדרה'

steps.title: What do you say?
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the 'exile' opinion, the speaker in the ברייתא asks רבי שמעון בן יוחי for his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: You, what do you say?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup line. רבי שמעון בן יוחי is asked for his view, and the next step gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question invites the opposing opinion. The disagreement is about whether the ארון left the בית המקדש at all.

phrases.english: You, what do you say?
phrases.notes: Addressed to רבי שמעון בן יוחי

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the 'exile' opinion to ask for the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's opinion on what happened to the ארון

steps.title: The ארון was hidden in its place
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי answers that the ארון was hidden away right where it stood. His source is the פסוק about the long poles of the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say that the ארון was hidden in its place, as it says: 'And the poles were long...' (ending with 'and they are there to this day').
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי gives the opposite view. The ארון never went into exile; it was buried and hidden on the spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is from מלכים א ח:ח, which describes the poles of the ארון. He only quotes the opening words ('וגו׳'). The key part is the ending, 'and they are there to this day,' which the next steps will discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: Was hidden away, stored out of sight
The poles used to carry the ארון
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the פסוק is implied

steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion, that the ארון is still hidden somewhere in the area of the מקדש, becomes the focus of the debate that follows.

phrases.english: He said to him: For I say:
The ark was hidden in its place,
as it says: 'And the poles were long, etc.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א ח:ח; the verse ends 'and they are there to this day'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with the opposing view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ארון was hidden in its place, based on the פסוק about the poles

steps.title: How does that verse prove it?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks עולא what in the פסוק about the poles shows that the ארון stayed in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to עולא: What in it implies this?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא itself (not the ברייתא) asks a question. רבה wants to know which words in the פסוק prove רבי שמעון בן יוחי's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, the פסוק only describes how long the poles were. It does not obviously say anything about the ארון being hidden, so רבה asks where the proof is.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it imply? How is this shown?

phrases.english: רבה said to עולא:
What is the implication? (How is this shown?)

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה לְעוּלָּא: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the פסוק cited in step 3 proves the claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words in מלכים א ח:ח show that the ארון was hidden in its place

steps.title: Because it says 'to this day'
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the proof is from the end of the פסוק: 'and they are there to this day.' He understands this to mean forever, whenever the פסוק is read.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they are there to this day.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא points to the words 'עד היום הזה'. He reads them as 'they are still there on any day you read this,' meaning the ארון never left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא takes 'to this day' as a permanent statement, true at all times. If the poles (and the ארון) are 'there' forever, then the ארון was never carried away but must be hidden on the spot.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And they are there to this day,'
phrases.notes: This is עולא's answer: 'to this day' means forever, on any day the פסוק is read.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיִּהְיוּ שָׁם עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'עד היום הזה' mean forever, so the ארון is still there

steps.title: Does 'to this day' always mean forever? The יבוסי case
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges עולא. The same phrase 'עד היום הזה' is used about the יבוסי living in ירושלים. Should we say they were never exiled?
steps.simpleTranslation: And wherever it is written 'to this day,' does it mean forever? But it is written: 'And the children of Binyamin did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, and the Jebusites lived with the children of Binyamin in Jerusalem to this day.' So should we also say they were never exiled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks עולא's reading of 'to this day.' He shows a פסוק where those same words cannot mean forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'עד היום הזה' always means forever, then the יבוסי must still be living in ירושלים and were never exiled. That is clearly not true, as the next steps will prove. So 'to this day' may only mean 'up to the time the פסוק was written,' and the proof for the ארון falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written?, introducing a contradicting פסוק
The Jebusites, a nation living in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the יבוסי really stayed. He is using an absurd result to show that 'to this day' cannot always mean forever.

phrases.english: And wherever it is written 'to this day,'
does it mean forever?
But isn't it written: 'And the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem'
phrases.notes: שופטים א:כא

phrases.english: the children of Binyamin did not drive out,
and the Jebusites lived with the children of Binyamin
in Jerusalem to this day'?
So here too, would you say they were not exiled?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב: עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה לְעוֹלָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's reading of 'עד היום הזה' given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that 'עד היום הזה' means forever
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same phrase is used about the יבוסי in ירושלים, who were certainly exiled, so the phrase cannot always mean forever.

steps.title: No one passed through יהודה for fifty-two years
steps.stepSummary: רבה proves that the יבוסי were exiled. He cites רבי יהודה's ברייתא that for fifty-two years after the חורבן no person passed through יהודה, hinted by the גימטריא of בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: רבי יהודה says, for fifty-two years no person passed through Judea, as it says: 'For the mountains I will raise crying and wailing, and for the pastures of the wilderness a lament, for they are burned, with no person passing through, and they do not hear the sound of cattle; from the bird of the heavens to the beast, they have fled and gone.' 'Beast' (בהמה) has the numerical value of fifty-two!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a ברייתא to back up his challenge. If the land was completely empty of people, then the יבוסי in ירושלים must also have been exiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו describes the land as totally abandoned. The word בהמה (ב=2, ה=5, מ=40, ה=5) adds up to 52, hinting at how many years it lasted. A land with nobody passing through cannot have יבוסי living in it, so 'עד היום הזה' about them did not mean forever.

keyTerms.meaning: By the numerical value of the letters

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: רבי יהודה says:
For fifty-two years
no person passed through Judea,
as it says: 'For the mountains I will raise crying and wailing,'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו ט:ט

phrases.english: and for the pastures of the wilderness a lament,
for they are burned, with no person passing through,
and they do not hear the sound of cattle;
from the bird of the heavens to the beast
they have fled and gone.'
'Beast' (בהמה) in numerical value
is fifty-two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's challenge in step 6 by proving the יבוסי were indeed exiled.
steps.raayaObject: The יבוסי were exiled from ירושלים, so 'עד היום הזה' does not mean forever
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהודה, based on ירמיהו ט:ט and the גימטריא of בהמה

steps.title: Brimstone and salt covered the land for seven years
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: רבי יוסי says that for seven years the land of ישראל was cursed with brimstone and salt, so it could not be lived in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי יוסי says, for seven years brimstone and salt remained in the land of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds another ברייתא to strengthen his point. The land was uninhabitable for years after the חורבן, so the יבוסי could not have stayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A land full of brimstone and salt cannot support people, like the curse described in פרשת נצבים (דברים כט:כב). This is another proof that everyone, the יבוסי included, left the land. The source for the 'seven years' comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Brimstone (sulfur) and salt, a curse that makes land barren

phrases.english: And it was taught: רבי יוסי says:
For seven years there remained
brimstone and salt in the land of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא supporting the same challenge as step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The land was uninhabitable after the חורבן, so the יבוסי were exiled

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: the word 'covenant' links two verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains רבי יוסי's source through a גזירה שוה on the word ברית. One פסוק links ברית with 'one week' (seven years). The other links ברית with the curse of brimstone and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: What is רבי יוסי's reason? It is learned from 'covenant'–'covenant.' It is written here: 'And he will make a firm covenant with many for one week,' and it is written there: 'And they will say: Because they forsook the covenant of ה׳, the God of their fathers.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows where רבי יוסי got 'seven years' of brimstone and salt. He links two פסוקים that both use the word ברית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דניאל, ברית appears with 'שבוע אחד,' one 'week' of years, which is seven years. In דברים, ברית appears in the curse of the land being 'brimstone and salt.' Because of the shared word, the seven years from the first פסוק are applied to the curse in the second. That gives seven years of an empty land, and the challenge to עולא stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?
It is written here / and it is written there, the standard formula of a גזירה שוה

steps.whatToRemember: רבה challenged עולא: 'עד היום הזה' cannot always mean forever, because the יבוסי were certainly exiled. רבי יהודה shows no one passed through יהודה for 52 years, and רבי יוסי (explained by רבי יוחנן) shows the land lay under brimstone and salt for 7 years.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'here' פסוק (דניאל) gives the length of time. The 'there' פסוק (דברים) gives the brimstone and salt. Neither פסוק alone says 'seven years of brimstone and salt'; only the link through ברית does.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:
What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
It is derived from 'covenant'–'covenant.'
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word shows up in two פסוקים, so we learn one from the other.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'And he will make a firm covenant with many'
phrases.notes: דניאל ט:כז

phrases.english: for one week' (seven years),
and it is written there: 'And they will say: Because they forsook'
phrases.notes: דברים כט:כד, in the passage describing the land as brimstone and salt

phrases.english: the covenant of ה׳, the God of their fathers'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for רבי יוסי's ברייתא in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's claim of seven years of brimstone and salt
steps.raayaSupportSource: גזירה שוה of 'ברית' between דניאל ט:כז and דברים כט:כד

steps.title: עולא answers that the word 'there' makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers רבה's challenge. The פסוק about the ארון says ״שָׁם״, but the פסוק about the יבוסי does not. Wherever ״שָׁם״ appears with ״עד היום הזה״, it means forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Here, about the ארון, it is written 'there.' There, about the יבוסי, 'there' is not written. And anywhere that 'there' is written, it means forever.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends his proof. He points out a word difference between the two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה showed that ״עד היום הזה״ alone cannot mean forever, because the יבוסי were exiled. עולא agrees about the יבוסי. But he says the ארון's פסוק has an extra word, ״שָׁם״, and that extra word is what turns the phrase into 'forever.'

phrases.english: He [Ulla] said to him [Rabbah]:
Here [about the Ark] 'there' is written,
there [about the Jebusites] 'there' is not written,
and anywhere that 'there' is written
phrases.notes: He means wherever 'there' is written together with 'to this day.'

phrases.english: it means forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכָא כְּתִיב ״שָׁם״, הָתָם לָא כְּתִיב ״שָׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge from the יבוסי (step 6) by finding a difference in wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the two cases (חילוק) based on an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase ״עד היום הזה״ alone was thought to mean forever, which the יבוסי case disproved.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ״שָׁם״ together with ״עד היום הזה״ means forever, and the ארון's פסוק has ״שָׁם״.

steps.title: A verse about the sons of Shimon also says 'there to this day'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא with a פסוק in דברי הימים. בני שמעון went to הר שעיר, struck עמלק, ״וישבו שם עד היום הזה״. This פסוק has both ״שָׁם״ and ״עד היום הזה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: 'And some of them, from the sons of Shimon, went to Mount Seir, five hundred men, with Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, at their head. And they struck the remaining survivors of Amalek, and they lived there to this day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק that has the exact wording עולא relies on. This sets up a challenge to his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said ״שָׁם״ plus ״עד היום הזה״ means forever. This פסוק has both words about בני שמעון living in הר שעיר. If עולא is right, בני שמעון should never have left that place. The next step shows that they did.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Seir, the region of Edom

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'And some of them, from the sons of Shimon,
went to Mount Seir
five hundred men,
and Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel,
the sons of Ishi, at their head.
And they struck the remaining survivors of Amalek,
and they lived there to this day.'
phrases.notes: Notice this פסוק has both 'there' and 'to this day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's new rule from step 10 with a פסוק that matches its exact wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that ״שָׁם״ with ״עד היום הזה״ means forever.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק with the same wording describes a people who did not stay forever, as the next step proves.

steps.title: Sennacherib already mixed up all the nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that בני שמעון did not stay in הר שעיר. סנחריב had already exiled and mixed up all the nations, as the פסוק in ישעיה says: 'I removed the borders of peoples.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But סנחריב king of Assyria had already come up and mixed up all the lands, as it says: 'And I removed the borders of peoples, and I plundered their treasures.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק about בני שמעון is a problem. בני שמעון were in fact exiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנחריב's policy was to move whole populations from place to place. So בני שמעון could not have stayed in הר שעיר forever. The פסוק still says ״וישבו שם עד היום הזה״. This shows that even ״שָׁם״ does not mean forever.

phrases.english: But Sennacherib king of Assyria had already come up
and mixed up all the lands,
phrases.notes: He moved nations from their homelands.

phrases.english: as it is said:
'And I removed the borders of peoples
and plundered their treasures.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְבָר עָלָה סַנְחֵרִיב מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר וּבִלְבֵּל כׇּל הָאֲרָצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא of step 11 by proving that בני שמעון were exiled.
steps.raayaObject: That בני שמעון did not remain in הר שעיר forever.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה י:יג, describing סנחריב's mixing of the nations.

steps.title: עולא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes with ״תיובתא״. עולא's rule about ״שָׁם״ is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that עולא's argument is defeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא has no answer to the בני שמעון פסוק. So his proof that the ארון stayed in its place forever, based on ״שָׁם עד היום הזה״, falls. The refutation is aimed at his proof from the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: ״עד היום הזה״, even with ״שָׁם״, does not prove that something lasts forever. So עולא's proof about the ארון is refuted.
steps.confusionAlert: The תיובתא knocks down עולא's proof from the פסוק. It does not by itself prove that the ארון was exiled. The very next step brings a view that the ארון was hidden in the מקדש.

phrases.english: This is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of steps 11-12 against עולא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's reading of ״שָׁם עד היום הזה״ as 'forever' is rejected.

steps.title: The חכמים say the ארון was hidden in the לשכת דיר העצים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a ברייתא: the חכמים say the ארון was hidden in the לשכת דיר העצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It was taught: And the חכמים say: the ארון was hidden in the Chamber of the Woodshed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source on where the ארון ended up. It quotes the view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the debate was whether the ארון was exiled or hidden. This ברייתא gives a specific location: the חכמים say it was hidden inside the מקדש, in the chamber where wood was stored. That is a different place from the קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: the Chamber of the Woodshed, where wood for the מזבח was stored

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
It was taught: And the Rabbis say:
the Ark, in the Chamber of the Woodshed
was hidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: תָּנָא, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After עולא's proof falls, the גמרא brings another tradition about the ארון's fate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the ארון was hidden in the לשכת דיר העצים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the ארון a concrete hiding place, which the next sources build on.

steps.title: A כהן found an odd floor tile and died before telling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says a משנה supports this. A כהן saw a floor tile that looked different from the others. He started to tell his friend but died before finishing. From this they knew for certain that the ארון was hidden there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this: There was a story with a כהן who was busy, and he saw a floor tile that was different from the others. He came and told his friend, but he did not manage to finish before his soul left him. So they knew for certain that the ארון was hidden there.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא brings a משנה that supports the חכמים's view about the ארון's hiding place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd tile hinted at a hidden opening under the floor. The כהן's sudden death showed that Heaven did not want the place revealed. That convinced everyone the ארון was really there. The story takes place in the woodshed chamber, so it matches the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: we too have learned (this in a משנה)
a floor tile that looked different

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
We too have also learned:
An incident with a certain priest who was busy [with something],
and he saw a floor tile different from the others,
and he came and told his friend,
but he did not manage to finish the matter
before his soul departed.
And they knew for certain that the Ark was hidden there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ברייתא of step 14 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the ארון was hidden in the לשכת דיר העצים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (שקלים ו) telling the story of the כהן and the odd floor tile.

steps.title: What was the priest doing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כהן was busy with when he noticed the tile.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he doing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the story's vague word ״מתעסק״. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the כהן was 'busy.' The גמרא wants to know what activity led him to discover the odd tile.

phrases.english: What was he doing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail in the story from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word ״מתעסק״ in the story refers to.

steps.title: He was working with his axe
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו answers that the כהן was busy with his axe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: He was busy with his axe.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו explains what the כהן was doing: working with his axe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While banging or working with the axe, he noticed that one tile sounded or looked different. That suggested a hollow space underneath.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥelbo said:
He was busy with his axe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ: מִתְעַסֵּק בְּקַרְדּוּמּוֹ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן was working with his axe.

steps.title: כהנים בעלי מומים sorting wood, an axe fell, and fire burst out
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל tells of two blemished כהנים checking wood for worms. One of them dropped his axe there, and a fire came out and consumed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Two כהנים with blemishes were checking wood for worms. The axe of one of them slipped and fell there, and fire came out and consumed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that confirms the axe detail and adds more to the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים בעלי מומים could not do the עבודה, so their job in the woodshed was to remove wormy wood that was not fit for the מזבח. The ברייתא supports רבי חלבו that an axe was involved. It also shows again that whoever came near the hiding place was punished, so the exact spot stayed secret.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught
priests with physical blemishes, unfit for the עבודה

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the ארון was hidden under the floor of the לשכת דיר העצים. Those who came near the spot died, so its exact location stayed hidden.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Two priests with blemishes
were checking the wood for worms,
and the axe of one of them slipped off
and fell there,
phrases.notes: On the spot where the ארון was hidden.

phrases.english: and fire came out and consumed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי חלבו's answer (step 17) that the כהן was working with an axe.
steps.raayaObject: That an axe was involved in discovering the ארון's hiding place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל about blemished כהנים in the woodshed.

steps.title: Two phrases in the same verse seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה points out that one פסוק says the ends of the בדים were seen, and the same פסוק says they were not seen outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה pointed out a contradiction. It is written: 'The ends of the poles were seen,' and it is written: 'But they were not seen outside.' So how can both be true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רב יהודה sets two phrases from the same פסוק against each other and asks how both can be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases come from the same verse in מלכים א about the ארון in the מקדש. One says the poles were visible and the other says they were not visible from outside. Read simply, they clash, so we need a way to make both true.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction (literally 'he threw' one source against another)
The poles used to carry the ארון
So how can this be? (a request to resolve a contradiction)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda raised a contradiction.
It is written: 'The ends of the poles were seen,'
phrases.notes: מלכים א ח:ח

phrases.english: and it is written: 'But they were not seen outside.'
phrases.notes: Same verse

phrases.english: How can this be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the ארון was hidden to how it stood in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two halves of מלכים א ח:ח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The poles cannot be both visible and invisible.

steps.title: They were seen and not seen at the same time
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the poles were partly visible: seen in one way, not seen in another.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were seen and they were not seen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה resolves his own contradiction. Both phrases are true, each in its own way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is short and leaves a question open: in what way were they seen, and in what way not? The ברייתא in the next step fills in the picture.

keyTerms.meaning: Seen and not seen, meaning partly visible

phrases.english: They were seen and not seen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both verses are true in different ways

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the poles moved but did not tear through
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses three phrases to rule out two extremes: the poles did not stay hidden, and they did not rip through the פרוכת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: 'The ends of the poles were seen.' You might think they did not move from their place. So the verse says: 'The poles were long.' You might think they tore through the curtain and came out. So the verse says: 'They were not seen outside.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב יהודה. It narrows the meaning step by step, using 'you might think' followed by 'the verse teaches.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first rules out the idea that the poles stayed put and stuck out nowhere, because 'they were long.' It then rules out the idea that they poked through the curtain, because 'they were not seen outside.' What remains is a middle position, which matches 'seen and not seen.'

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (introduces support)
The verse teaches (to reject that idea)
The curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: This was also taught in a baraita:
'The ends of the poles were seen,'
one might think they did not move from their place,
so the verse says: 'The poles were long.'
One might think they tore through the curtain and came out,
so the verse says: 'They were not seen outside.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's answer 'seen and not seen'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the phrases of מלכים א ח:ח

steps.title: The poles pressed against the curtain like a woman's breasts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains what the poles looked like: they pushed against the פרוכת and made two bulges, and it supports this with a פסוק from שיר השירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So how was it? The poles pushed and bulged out against the curtain, and they looked like a woman's two breasts, as it says: 'My beloved is to me a bundle of myrrh that rests between my breasts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by describing exactly how the poles were both seen and not seen. They pushed the curtain outward without tearing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From outside you saw two bulges in the curtain but not the poles themselves. That is 'seen' and 'not seen' at once. The פסוק from שיר השירים links the image to the love between ה׳ and כלל ישראל, with the שכינה resting 'between' the two.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle of myrrh (שיר השירים א:יג)

steps.whatToRemember: The poles were seen and not seen. They pushed the פרוכת outward into two bulges but never broke through.

phrases.english: How was it?
They pushed, bulged, and stuck out against the curtain,
and looked like a woman's two breasts,
as it says: 'My beloved is to me a bundle of myrrh'
'that rests between my breasts.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by describing the middle position it reached.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Physical description that fits both phrases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either fully hidden or fully poking through
steps.terutzMaskana: They made visible bulges in the curtain without coming through

steps.title: On the רגל the כרובים were shown to the people
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא says that when the people came up for the רגל, the כהנים rolled back the פרוכת and showed them the כרובים embracing, as a sign of ה׳'s love.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: When ישראל came up for the festival, they would roll up the curtain for them and show them the כרובים, which were embracing each other, and say to them: 'See how beloved you are before ה׳, like the love of a male and female.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the theme of love with a new statement from רב קטינא about showing the כרובים to the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea moves from the poles to the כרובים themselves. The embracing כרובים stood for the closeness between ה׳ and כלל ישראל, and the people were shown this openly on the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: Going up to ירושלים for a pilgrimage festival
The golden winged figures on top of the ארון
Your belovedness, ה׳'s love for you

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the opening of the ארון itself. Only the פרוכת curtain was rolled back so the people could see the כרובים.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
When the Jewish people would go up for the festival,
they would roll up the curtain for them,
and show them the cherubs,
which were clinging to one another,
and they would say to them:
See how beloved you are before God,
like the love of a male and female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the love imagery from the poles to the כרובים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the רגל the כרובים were displayed to the people behind a rolled-back פרוכת.

steps.title: Even the לויים could not look at the holy vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects: the תורה forbids looking at the holy כלים even while they are being packed, so how could the people be shown the כרובים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: 'They shall not come in to see the holy things as they are being covered,' and רב יהודה said in the name of רב that this refers to when the vessels were put into their cases. So how could the people be shown them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רב קטינא's statement with a פסוק that forbids looking at the holy vessels. The גמרא will need to answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the ban applies even when the כלים are being wrapped for travel, a less holy moment. It should apply all the more when they stand in their place in the קודש הקדשים. So showing the כרובים to the whole nation seems forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: When the holy things are being covered (wrapped up)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of how a display of the כרובים could be allowed, which the גמרא goes on to answer.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda raised an objection:
'They shall not come in to see'
phrases.notes: במדבר ד:כ

phrases.english: 'the holy things as they are being covered,'
and Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
This refers to when the vessels are put into their cases!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב קטינא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב קטינא's claim that the כרובים were shown to the people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if looking at the כלים while they are being packed is forbidden, looking at them in their holy place is surely forbidden.

steps.title: The parable of the bride
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רב חסדא with a parable. A bride is modest in her father's house but not once she lives in her husband's home. So in the מדבר the holy כלים were hidden, but in the בית המקדש they could be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It is like a bride. As long as she is in her father's house, she is modest before her husband. Once she comes to her father-in-law's house, she is no longer modest before him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רב חסדא's question from Step 24. He uses a parable to show why looking was forbidden in the מדבר but allowed in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against looking at the holy כלים applied in the מדבר, when the שכינה had no permanent home. That is like a bride who is engaged but still lives with her father. Once the שכינה 'moved in' to its permanent home in the בית המקדש, the closeness was complete, so showing the כרובים was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Modest, keeping herself covered or reserved
Her father-in-law's house, meaning her married home

steps.confusionAlert: The parable is not about the כלים themselves changing. It is about the relationship: the מדבר was like the engagement stage, and the בית המקדש was like the marriage.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
It is like a bride;
as long as she is in her father's house
she is modest before her husband.
phrases.notes: This matches the מדבר, where seeing the כלים was forbidden.

phrases.english: Once she comes to her father-in-law's house
she is not modest before her husband.
phrases.notes: This matches the בית המקדש, where the כרובים could be shown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's objection from Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between time periods, explained through a parable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on seeing the holy כלים applies at all times
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applied only in the temporary stage of the מדבר. In the permanent בית המקדש, seeing was allowed.

steps.title: Challenge from the כהן who found the ארון's hiding place
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר רב קטינא objects from the משנה about a כהן who discovered where the ארון was hidden and died. This suggests that seeing the holy objects was forbidden even after the בית המקדש was built.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר רב קטינא raised an objection: There was an incident with a certain כהן who was busy, and so on!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא בר רב קטינא challenges רב נחמן's answer. He cites a story from the משנה that seems to show the holy objects were still hidden in the time of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that story, a כהן working in the בית המקדש noticed the spot where the ארון was hidden, and he died before he could reveal it. If seeing were allowed in the בית המקדש, why was the ארון kept hidden from him? This seems to contradict the bride parable.

keyTerms.meaning: Busy or occupied with a task
Etc.; the rest of the quoted source is assumed known

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב חָנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Rav Ketina raised an objection:
There was an incident with a certain kohen
who was busy, etc.!
phrases.notes: He noticed an odd floor stone where the ארון was hidden, and he died before he could tell anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב חָנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's answer in Step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that seeing the holy objects was allowed in the בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows that the hidden ארון was kept from view even during the time of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: After the divorce, the old modesty returns
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the story of the כהן took place after the 'divorce,' meaning after the exile and the loss of the מקדש ראשון. A divorced woman goes back to her earlier reserved state, so the holy objects were hidden again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are speaking of when she was divorced. Once she is divorced, she goes back to her first state of affection.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenge by extending his own parable. The story of the כהן happened in a later period, after the closeness was broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן lived in the time of the מקדש שני, after the חורבן of the מקדש ראשון. כלל ישראל was like a wife sent away by her husband, so the relationship went back to its earlier, more reserved stage. That is why the ארון stayed hidden then, while in the מקדש ראשון the כרובים could be shown.

keyTerms.meaning: She was divorced; here, a picture of the exile
Her first affection, meaning the earlier reserved stage like engagement
You are saying / you are talking about

phrases.english: He said to him:
You are speaking of when she was divorced;
once divorced, she returns to her first affection.
phrases.notes: The reserved, modest stage comes back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between time periods, extending the same parable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hidden ארון shows that seeing was always forbidden in the בית המקדש
steps.terutzMaskana: Hiding came back only after the exile; in the time of the full closeness, seeing was allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Three stages: the מדבר is like engagement (hidden), the מקדש ראשון is like marriage (shown), and after the exile is like divorce (hidden again).

steps.title: Which מקדש did רב קטינא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב קטינא's statement. The מקדש ראשון had a wall, not a פרוכת, before the קודש הקדשים, and the מקדש שני had no כרובים. So neither period seems to fit his description.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If we say the מקדש ראשון, was there a פרוכת? But if it is the מקדש שני, were there כרובים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב קטינא's statement from Step 23 and asks when it could have happened. Each choice seems to be missing something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש ראשון, a wall separated the היכל from the קודש הקדשים, so there was no פרוכת to roll back. In the מקדש שני, the ארון and its כרובים were gone. Either way, the picture of 'rolling back the פרוכת to show the כרובים' seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with?
If we say in the First Temple,
was there a curtain?
phrases.notes: No. A wall stood there instead.

phrases.english: Rather, in the Second Temple,
were there כרובים?
phrases.notes: No. The ארון was already hidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִי נֵימָא בְּמִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bride discussion and returns to examine רב קטינא's statement in Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רב קטינא's statement about rolling back the פרוכת to show the כרובים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: the מקדש ראשון had no פרוכת, and the מקדש שני had no כרובים.

steps.title: מקדש ראשון, and the פרוכת of the gates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב קטינא meant the מקדש ראשון. The 'פרוכת' was not one inside the היכל but the curtains hanging on the gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it was in the מקדש ראשון. And what is the 'פרוכת'? The curtain of the gates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the dilemma by choosing the מקדש ראשון and reading the word 'פרוכת' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרובים existed in the מקדש ראשון, so that part fits. The problem was the missing פרוכת, so the גמרא explains that רב קטינא meant the curtains on the outer gates. Those were rolled up so the crowds could see inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth; keeps the first option and defends it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture the famous פרוכת in front of the קודש הקדשים. Here 'פרוכת' means the curtains on the gates.

phrases.english: Actually, in the First Temple,
and what is the 'curtain'?
The curtain of the gates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'פרוכת' means the curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים
steps.terutzMaskana: 'פרוכת' means the gate curtains of the מקדש ראשון

steps.title: Thirteen פרוכות in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea of gate curtains with רבי זירא in the name of רב. There were thirteen curtains in the מקדש: seven for seven gates, one each at the entrances of the היכל and the אולם, two in the דביר, and two matching them in the upper chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זירא said in the name of רב: There were thirteen curtains in the מקדש. Seven were opposite the seven gates. Two more: one at the entrance of the היכל and one at the entrance of the אולם. Two were in the דביר, and two matching them were in the upper chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that gates in the מקדש really had curtains. This backs up the answer in Step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list shows that the term 'פרוכת' was used for gate curtains, not only for the curtain before the קודש הקדשים. רב's list describes the מקדש שני, but it is assumed the gates had curtains in the מקדש ראשון too.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The inner area of the קודש הקדשים

steps.whatToRemember: רב קטינא's 'פרוכת' refers to gate curtains in the מקדש ראשון, and רב's list of thirteen curtains shows that such gate curtains existed.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav:
There were thirteen curtains in the Temple:
seven opposite seven gates,
phrases.notes: These are the gate curtains that support Step 29.

phrases.english: two: one at the entrance of the Sanctuary,
and one at the entrance of the Entrance Hall.
two in the inner chamber,
phrases.notes: In the מקדש שני, these replaced the separating wall.

phrases.english: and two matching them in the upper chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the 'gate curtain' answer of Step 29
steps.raayaObject: That the gates of the מקדש had curtains called פרוכת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא in the name of רב: thirteen curtains, seven of them at the gates

steps.title: The statement refers to the מקדש שני and its pictured כרובים
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that רב קטינא meant the מקדש שני. That מקדש did have a פרוכת, and its כרובים were carved images on the walls. He proves from a פסוק that the walls had carved כרובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Really, רב קטינא was talking about the מקדש שני. There were כרובים there in the form of pictures. As it is written: 'And all the walls of the house round about he carved with carved figures of כרובים, palm trees, and open flowers, and he overlaid them with gold fitted upon the carved work.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different answer to the question from Step 28. He says רב קטינא was speaking about the מקדש שני after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that the מקדש שני had no כרובים. רב אחא answers that it had no solid golden כרובים, but it did have carved pictures of כרובים on the walls. So both details fit the מקדש שני: it had a real פרוכת, and it had כרובים in picture form.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. It returns to an option that was set aside earlier.
A form or picture, meaning an image and not a solid object
The engraved surface that the gold was fitted onto

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse two kinds of כרובים. The golden כרובים on the ארון were missing in the מקדש שני. The כרובים in this answer are only carved pictures on the walls.

Actually, it refers to the Second Temple,

phrases.notes: These were pictures on the walls, not the solid golden כרובים.

phrases.notes: מלכים א ו:לה. The גמרא joins phrases from two nearby פסוקים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בְּמִקְדָּשׁ שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in Step 28, instead of the gate-curtain answer in Steps 29-30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the term: the 'כרובים' are carved pictures, not the golden כרובים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקדש שני had no כרובים at all, so רב קטינא could not have meant it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקדש שני had a פרוכת and carved pictures of כרובים on the walls, so רב קטינא's statement fits it.

steps.title: A second verse about the carved figures
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא adds another פסוק that describes the carved figures with the words כמער איש ולויות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'Like the space of a man and wreaths.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא brings a second פסוק about the carvings. This verse sets up the next question about what its unusual words mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק showed that carved כרובים existed. This second פסוק adds a detail about how the figures looked. Its meaning is unclear, so the גמרא will need to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the space of a man. The figures were set close together, each by the other.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'According to the space of each, with wreaths.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א ז:לו

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to רב אחא's proof.

steps.title: What does 'like the space of a man and wreaths' mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כמער איש ולויות means. It introduces רבה בר רב שילא, whose answer appears on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like the space of a man and wreaths' mean? רבה בר רב שילא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear words in the פסוק. It then names רבה בר רב שילא, who will explain them right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question asking for an explanation. It is not an attack on רב אחא. The answer will describe how the carved figures were shaped and placed.
